title: Showing What You Can Do
description: Present your work so someone can tell in two minutes that you can build things: what reviewers actually scan for, how to write a project page around the decisions you made rather than the tools you used, how to describe a project honestly without underselling it, cleaning code enough that a stranger can follow it, and why three finished projects beat thirty abandoned ones.

title: Learning the Next Thing
description: Learn a new tool or framework on your own, without a course: reading documentation for the one thing you actually need instead of top to bottom, learning by building the smallest real slice instead of finishing someone else's tutorial, telling a genuine learning need apart from hype, weighing what a framework actually buys you against what it costs, and recognizing when you know enough to start.

title: Working With Other People
description: Collaborate on code without meetings, and take feedback on your work: opening a pull request someone can review without asking you what it does, receiving a critical review without it landing as a judgment of you, reviewing someone else's code kindly and usefully, making a first real contribution to an open source project, and collaborating asynchronously on your own hours.

title: Getting Paid for This
description: Understand the realistic routes from this skill to money, and their trade-offs: employed, freelance, and product work compared honestly on odds and demands; decoding what a junior role actually requires versus what it lists; landing small, scoped, real first paid work; pricing a first job sensibly at variable capacity; and naming that capacity to a client professionally.

title: Keeping Going
description: Build a practice that survives bad weeks, long gaps and losing momentum: safely resuming a project after a month away, structuring projects so future-you can pick them up cold, handling the comparison problem instead of being flattened by it, finding people to learn alongside without needing live meetups, and writing down what you'd actually tell yourself at lesson one.
